# Vendored AxBench

This directory contains a focused source snapshot of
[stanfordnlp/axbench](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/axbench) at commit
`41c8332543e5a631f9a8c0a9df38799893ace758`.

AxBench is licensed under Apache-2.0; see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). The repository's
top-level MIT license does not replace the license for this subtree.

## Contents

The initial snapshot retained the upstream Python 3.12 declaration,
`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, license, README, and 62 Python files that make up
the runtime package. Its 67 retained upstream files were byte-identical to the
recorded commit before the narrow compatibility changes listed below.

The snapshot deliberately omits upstream notebooks, historical sweep files,
tests, demos, data-download helpers, committed result Parquets and state files,
generated pages, caches, datasets, and virtual environments. The local
`prepare.py` and the sweep configs under `axbench/sweep/nano_gpt_pretrain_steer/`
are additions for this repository; generated data lives under the top-level
`out/axbench/` directory.

## Environment

AxBench has a separate Python 3.12 environment. Do not install its dependencies
into the root project environment.

```bash
uv sync --project vendor/axbench --frozen
uv run --project vendor/axbench --frozen python --version
uv run --project vendor/axbench --frozen python vendor/axbench/prepare.py
```

The lock declares Stanza and resolves the upstream `pyvene>=0.1.8` requirement.
Run AxBench entry points through
`python -m scripts.eval.axbench_upstream.run_baselines`; the launcher selects
this environment with `uv run --project vendor/axbench --frozen`.

The lock selects PyTorch 2.7.1+cu128 from the explicit PyTorch CUDA 12.8
index on Linux and Windows; other platforms retain PyPI as their source.
This supplies Blackwell support to normal frozen workers. Transformers
5.16.1, PyVene 0.1.8, and PEFT 0.13.2 retain their existing locked versions.
See the [GCG GPU qualification](../../docs/performance/axbench-adv-gcg.md#blackwell-qualification)
for the tested hardware, numerical comparisons, and environment receipts.

## Local modifications

Unlike `nanochat/`, this vendored subtree may receive narrow, reviewed fixes
needed by the AxBench pipeline. Keep each change small, preserve upstream
notices, add a prominent modification notice to changed upstream files, and
record it here.

| Change | Paths | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Initial snapshot | None of the 67 retained upstream files | Vendor only the runtime source and isolated environment metadata |
| Dependency repair | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Declare Stanza, pin its package, and resolve PyVene consistently |
| Blackwell-capable worker environment | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Select PyTorch 2.7.1 with CUDA 12.8 for Linux and Windows frozen workers. Update its CUDA, Triton, and SymPy dependencies while retaining other package versions. Qualify real GCG worker paths on Blackwell and numerical parity on Hopper. |
| Lazy optional services | `axbench/scripts/evaluate.py`, `axbench/scripts/inference.py` | Initialize Stanza lazily, use prepared resources without downloading when configured, and create an OpenAI-compatible OpenRouter client only for methods, datasets, or fallback data generation that need it |
| Qwen chat handling | `axbench/utils/constants.py`, `axbench/utils/model_utils.py`, `axbench/utils/dataset.py`, `axbench/models/hypernet/utils.py`, `axbench/models/model.py`, `axbench/models/prompt.py`, `axbench/models/reft.py`, `axbench/scripts/train.py`, `axbench/scripts/inference.py` | Register Qwen, remove only a BOS token that was actually emitted, retain its opening chat marker, align latent token labels with encoded inputs, and avoid appending a new assistant-generation prompt to completed training turns |
| Bounded and resumable inference | `axbench/scripts/inference.py` | Apply `max_concepts` to every metadata load, reject requests beyond the available rows, keep empty ranks in DDP synchronization, and save latent resume state in the directory from which it is loaded |
| Strict steering scale | `axbench/models/model.py`, `axbench/scripts/inference.py` | Require the latent-stage output and raise when a selected concept has no computed `max_act` instead of silently using `1.0` |
| Local pipeline inputs | `prepare.py`, `axbench/sweep/nano_gpt_pretrain_steer/*.yaml` | Download pinned input datasets/resources with a bounded metadata request, support a safely bounded preparation directory and force rebuild, and configure the four optional baseline methods for Qwen; project-only input production stays in the root environment and loads no Qwen model |
| OpenRouter provider routing | `axbench/utils/openrouter.py`, `axbench/scripts/inference.py`, `axbench/scripts/generate.py`, `axbench/utils/dataset.py`, `axbench/models/language_models.py` | Use `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` through OpenRouter for PromptSteering synthesis and other vendored LM-backed data paths; read `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and optional `OPENROUTER_BASE_URL` |
| Optional AxBench-Adv pilot spending fence | `axbench/utils/openrouter.py`, `axbench/scripts/evaluate.py` | When `AXBENCH_ADV_PILOT_BUDGET_FILE` is set, install root-owned HTTPX hooks in both worker and final-judge clients; reserve a conservatively priced full request in one shared SQLite ledger before every actual SDK attempt, including retries. Unknown costs retain their reservation. Requests, cache keys, key limits, and the unset client behavior are unchanged. |
| Strict cached judge evaluation | `axbench/evaluators/lm_judge.py`, `axbench/evaluators/judge_cache.py`, `axbench/models/language_models.py`, `axbench/scripts/args/eval_args.py`, `axbench/scripts/evaluate.py`, `axbench/sweep/nano_gpt_pretrain_steer/evaluate.yaml` | Judge only declared method/factor cells, reject malformed ratings, add bounded single-layer retries, share exact requests through a small SQLite cache with a read-only cache-only mode, and emit the evaluator's exact call/cache-hit counters as JSON |
| Diagnosable judge-worker failures | `axbench/scripts/evaluate.py` | Execute `num_of_workers=1` tasks in the launcher process so provider exceptions retain their original object and traceback; for multi-worker runs, wrap failures at the process boundary in a picklable error carrying status, task coordinates, and the formatted original traceback. Validate worker counts before side effects, keep executor shutdown lexical, and preserve a primary failure when cleanup also fails. |
| Retry-After ruling conformance | `axbench/models/language_models.py` | Honor a server-sent judge `Retry-After` verbatim instead of silently capping it, with escalating `warning`/`error` log bands above 60s/300s (issue #1313 owner ruling); the headerless exponential-backoff fallback keeps its existing 60s cap |
| Attacked steering-input override | `axbench/scripts/args/dataset_args.py`, `axbench/scripts/inference.py` | Add `--overwrite_steering_input_parquet` so AxBench-Adv can replace generated steering inputs with a validated frame containing exactly one row per configured concept/input cell, whose single factor matches the configured cell. Invalid SAE references raise, state and ranked outputs use the effective override dump directory, and the unset path preserves ordinary AxBench data construction (not byte-identical diagnostic stdout, which includes the optional argument). |
| Shared AxBench-Adv generation runtime | `axbench/scripts/inference.py`, `axbench/models/model.py`, `axbench/models/lora.py`, `axbench/utils/model_utils.py` | Route ordinary inference and the persistent AxBench-Adv worker through one exact `predict_steer` call, and let generation progress bars use rank zero when no distributed process group exists. Ordinary DDP rank behavior is unchanged. |
| AxBench-Adv generation-only prediction | `axbench/scripts/inference.py`, `axbench/models/lora.py`, `axbench/models/prompt.py` | Let the AxBench-Adv worker skip LoRA and PromptSteering's unused post-generation perplexity forward pass. Ordinary AxBench prediction retains perplexity by default, and generation runs before the optional branch. |
| Six-method judged model list | `axbench/sweep/nano_gpt_pretrain_steer/evaluate.yaml` | Add `SelfConditioningMasked` to the judged `models` list so the vendored evaluator scores both root-environment project methods alongside the four Qwen baselines |
| Ten-method judged model list | `axbench/sweep/nano_gpt_pretrain_steer/evaluate.yaml` | Add the four encoder-decoder baseline analogs to the judged `models` list so the vendored evaluator scores them alongside the existing six methods |
| GPT-NeoX component resolution | `axbench/models/mean.py`, `axbench/models/probe.py`, `axbench/utils/model_utils.py` | Resolve the DiffMean/LinearProbe steering component and `gather_residual_activations`'s decoder-layer list by `config.model_type` instead of a Llama/Qwen-only literal `model.layers[...]` path, so GPT-NeoX-family targets (Pythia) resolve via pyvene's `block_output`/`.gpt_neox.layers` instead of raising `AttributeError`; also skip `get_suffix_length`'s chat-template probe for tokenizers with no chat template (every caller only consumes its result inside an `is_chat_model` branch), fixing a `ValueError` that fired unconditionally in `prepare_df` regardless of `is_chat_model`. Every currently-supported model keeps its exact prior behavior; only the new `gpt_neox` branch and the no-template short-circuit are additive. |
| GPT-NeoX pad-token fallback | `axbench/scripts/train.py`, `axbench/scripts/inference.py` | Broaden the fallback-pad-token condition from `unk_token is None and pad_token is None` (a `# raw llama3`-specific check) to `pad_token is None` alone, so GPT-NeoX-family tokenizers (Pythia: `unk_token` set, `pad_token` unset) also get a usable pad token instead of `RuntimeError: Could not infer dtype of NoneType` in the training collator. Every currently-supported model already has a real `pad_token`, so this branch still never fires for them. |
| GPT-NeoX fast-tokenizer steering load | `axbench/scripts/inference.py` | `infer_steering`'s tokenizer load hardcodes `use_fast=False`; GPT-NeoX-family models ship no slow tokenizer class at all (`ValueError: Tokenizer class GPTNeoXTokenizer does not exist`), so load fast (`use_fast=True`) specifically for them. Every other model keeps its existing `use_fast=False` load. |
| Base-model AlpacaEval steering prompts | `axbench/utils/dataset.py` | `SteeringDatasetFactory.create_eval_df`'s `AlpacaEval` branch called `apply_chat_template` unconditionally (no `is_chat_model`-style gate at all, unlike every other templating call site in this vendored subtree), raising for any tokenizer with no chat template. Gate on `self.tokenizer.chat_template`; a base model uses the raw prompt/steering text directly, matching the no-template convention used elsewhere (e.g. `prepare_df`'s non-chat branch). Every chat-model tokenizer takes the exact prior path unchanged. |
| Pythia-2.8B base-model sweep | `axbench/sweep/nano_gpt_pretrain_steer/pythia_2_8b_main.yaml`, `axbench/sweep/nano_gpt_pretrain_steer/pythia_2_8b_aux.yaml` | Configure the four baseline methods for `EleutherAI/pythia-2.8b` as a base-model (not chat-model) comparison point; layer choices scaled from the Qwen sweep's layer 28 / `[7, 14, 21, 28]` of 36 decoder layers to Pythia's 32, and `lora_components` set to GPT-NeoX's `dense` attention-output projection name (Qwen/Llama use `o_proj`) |
| Retry a malformed (no-`choices`) judge response | `axbench/models/language_models.py` | A live judge HTTP response can come back 200 OK with an error body (`{"error": {...}}`) instead of a completion -- e.g. a transient OpenRouter provider failure or no provider available -- which the OpenAI SDK does not always surface as a raised exception. `_live_completion` previously accessed `payload["choices"][0]` unguarded, so this raised a bare, unretried `KeyError` that aborted the entire (paid, multi-hour) judge run on a single transient response. Detected explicitly and raised as the new `MalformedLanguageModelResponseError`, retried the same as `EmptyLanguageModelResponseError` (up to `MAX_TOTAL_ATTEMPTS`); the terminal error message includes the payload's `error` field. First observed on the Pythia-2.8B c50 baseline judge run, 2026-08-27, after ~26 concepts had already completed successfully. |
| Baseline-only (four-method) judged model list | `axbench/sweep/nano_gpt_pretrain_steer/baseline_evaluate.yaml` | A copy of `evaluate.yaml` scoped to just `[DiffMean, LinearProbe, PromptSteering, LoRA]`, for judging a base model (e.g. Pythia) that the project's SAE-conditioning and encoder-decoder methods do not apply to. Consumed by `scripts/eval/axbench_upstream/merge_baseline_methods.py` and `run_baseline_evaluation.py`, which mirror `merge_methods.py`/`run_evaluation.py` scoped to the four vendored methods; `merge_methods.py`'s `validate_steering_frame`/`read_canonical_merged_frame` gained an additive `methods` override for `source="merged"` (previously `project`-only) and an additive `max_blank_fraction` override (default unchanged) so both share the same reviewed validation contract. The blank-generation tripwire's owner-ratified 1% bound was calibrated on chat-tuned-model (Qwen) runs; a Pythia-2.8B c50 run legitimately blanked 1.5% of LinearProbe cells (including at `factor=0.0`, no steering -- honest base-model sampling, not collapse: median generation length stayed healthy and DiffMean showed the same zero-steering blank rate on different rows). `merge_baseline_methods.BASELINE_MAX_BLANK_GENERATION_FRACTION = 0.02` documents this separately-calibrated bound for base-model runs; owner approved 2026-08-27. |
| Transformers bump for SmolLM3 support | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `axbench/__init__.py`, `axbench/models/sae.py` | Bump `transformers` from `>=4.42.4` (locked 4.45.1) to `>=4.53.0` (locked 5.16.1; SmolLM3 support was added in 4.53.0), needed to add SmolLM3-3B as a baseline target. `pyreft>=0.0.8` hard-pinned `transformers==4.45.1` with no compatible newer release across every published pyreft version, so it is dropped (also removing a large unrelated transitive dependency tree pyreft alone pulled in: `ydata-profiling` and a Google Cloud Storage stack). `axbench/__init__.py` stops eagerly importing `reft.py`/`concept_reft.py`/`preference_reft.py`/`ig.py` (import pyreft) and `hypersteer.py`/`hypernet/{layers,modeling_hypernet}.py` (hand-fork Gemma-2 internals via a private `transformers.models.gemma2.modeling_gemma2` symbol removed by the bump); none are used by any active config, their source is unchanged and still directly importable, and `axbench/models/sae.py` drops one genuinely unused `import pyreft`. Verified in an isolated scratch copy before applying for real: dependency resolution, `import axbench`, pyvene intervention hooking, peft LoRA injection, and all three entry-point scripts (`train.py`/`inference.py`/`evaluate.py --help`) all pass; ReFT/ConceptReFT/PreferenceReFT/IG/HyperSteer become unavailable until pyreft/the hypernet code are updated upstream. |
| Decoder-layer hook tuple-unwrapping | `axbench/utils/model_utils.py` | `gather_residual_activations`'s forward hook unconditionally did `target_act = outputs[0]`, assuming a decoder layer's forward always returns a tuple `(hidden_states, ...)`. Under transformers 5.16.1, every architecture tested (GPT-NeoX and Llama-family) instead returns the hidden-states tensor directly, so `outputs[0]` silently indexed into the BATCH dimension instead of unwrapping a tuple -- corrupting the collected activations for every consumer (`DiffMean`/`MeanActivation` in `mean.py`, `LinearProbe` in `probe.py`, `LoRA` in `lora.py`) for ANY model, not just one architecture. Caught by a live GPU regression run (`IndexError: mask shape does not match indexed tensor`) after the transformers bump above, despite prior isolated verification (a direct pyvene intervention forward pass, which does not go through this function, had passed). Fixed with `outputs[0] if isinstance(outputs, (tuple, list)) else outputs`, handling both conventions; re-verified with a direct shape check plus a full 5-stage Pythia-2.8B c2 GPU run (main train/latent/steering, aux train/steering) covering all four baseline methods. |
| `apply_chat_template` BatchEncoding unwrapping | `axbench/utils/model_utils.py`, `axbench/scripts/train.py`, `axbench/scripts/inference.py` | Under transformers 5.16.1, `tokenizer.apply_chat_template(..., tokenize=True)` returns a `BatchEncoding` (dict-like) instead of a plain list of token ids. Every call site in this vendored subtree that treats the result as a plain list was written before this change, and the failure mode is NOT uniformly a crash: `reversed(BatchEncoding)` raises `TypeError` (`get_suffix_length`, caught first, on the first SmolLM3 chat-model run under the bump -- this code path is unreached by any base model, which is why the earlier Pythia-only regression testing after the transformers bump above did not catch it), but `zip(BatchEncoding, BatchEncoding)` and `len(BatchEncoding)` do NOT raise -- they silently iterate/count the dict's KEYS (`"input_ids"`, `"attention_mask"`) instead of token ids, so `get_prefix_length`'s no-common-prefix branch silently returned `0` instead of the correct chat-template prefix length (confirmed directly: Qwen's correct value is 24, the buggy `zip` loop returns 0 every time, since both sequences share the same two key names) -- a defect a full training run would NOT have crashed on, only produced corrupted (but plausible-looking) results, exactly the failure class this project treats as more serious than a crash. Fixed at the three points reachable by the four active baseline methods: `get_suffix_length` and `get_prefix_length` (both branches) now index `["input_ids"]` immediately after each `apply_chat_template` call; `strip_leading_bos` (called directly by `dataset.py`'s six AlpacaEval-prompt sites, `prompt.py`'s PromptSteering relevance-judging site, and transitively via `strip_chat_template_tokens` from `train.py`'s `prepare_df` and `inference.py`'s `prepare_df`) now unwraps a `BatchEncoding` at its single entry point rather than requiring each of those ~10 call sites to be patched individually. `data_utils.py`'s `get_prompt_suffix_length` has the same `reversed()` defect and was NOT fixed -- it does have real callers (`preprocess_preference_data`, invoked from `make_preference_data_module`, imported by `preference_model.py`/`preference_reft.py`/`preference_lora.py`/`concept_model.py`), but none of those call chains are reachable from any active config (no `Preference*` method is ever configured, so `make_preference_data_module` is never invoked); noted here rather than silently left for whoever enables a preference method later. |
| Baseline-only (five-method) judged model list | `axbench/sweep/nano_gpt_pretrain_steer/baseline_selfcond_evaluate.yaml` | A copy of `evaluate.yaml` scoped to `[DiffMean, LinearProbe, PromptSteering, LoRA, SelfConditioning]`, for a base model's four vendored baselines plus the project's own SelfConditioning method alone -- deliberately excluding SelfConditioningMasked until its rank-based candidate-pool rewrite (`..._sign_rank_v3`, PR #1592) has its own project-methods data regenerated and separately validated, so it is not judged against stale or unvalidated data. Consumed by `scripts/eval/axbench_upstream/merge_baseline_selfcond_methods.py` and `run_baseline_selfcond_evaluation.py`, the five-method siblings of the four-method and six-method pairs above. |
| SmolLM3 chat-template date pin | `axbench/utils/model_utils.py` | SmolLM3's chat template embeds the wall-clock date in its default system prompt (`{%- set today = strftime_now("%d %B %Y") -%}`), and `apply_chat_template` exposes no parameter to override it. A c50 run's main config (rendered 2026-08-27) and aux config (rendered 2026-08-28, the run having crossed a calendar-day boundary) therefore produced textually different -- though semantically identical -- prompts for the same concept, failing the merge's input-matching check (owner-reported: "Did you run all the evaluations with the current date in the system prompt? Can we remove the date?"). Each of the two branches was internally self-consistent (fit and evaluated together, same rendered date throughout), so only the cross-branch date differed. `render_jinja_template`'s compiled Jinja environment binds `strftime_now` to a closure over `chat_template_utils`'s module-level `datetime.now()`; substituting a `datetime.datetime` subclass with a frozen `.now()` into that one module's namespace pins every future render (Qwen's and Pythia's templates never call `strftime_now`, so they are unaffected) without touching any other `datetime` consumer, including this package's own logging timestamps. Pinned to 2026-08-27 to match the already-generated (9-GPU-hour) main branch, so only aux needed regenerating rather than the whole c50 run. |
| Baseline-plus-project (six-method) judged model list | `axbench/sweep/nano_gpt_pretrain_steer/baseline_project_evaluate.yaml` | A copy of `evaluate.yaml` scoped to `[DiffMean, LinearProbe, PromptSteering, LoRA, SelfConditioning, SelfConditioningMasked]`, for judging a base model's four vendored baselines alongside the project's own encoder-decoder conditioning methods, with no encoder-decoder baseline analogs (unlike the ten-method comparison, which targets a chat model like Qwen and includes `EncDec*`). Consumed by `scripts/eval/axbench_upstream/merge_baseline_project_methods.py` and `run_baseline_project_evaluation.py`, the six-method siblings of the four-method `merge_baseline_methods.py`/`run_baseline_evaluation.py` pair and the ten-method `merge_methods.py`/`run_evaluation.py` pair, reusing the same `validate_steering_frame`/`read_canonical_merged_frame` `methods`/`max_blank_fraction` override machinery. Built for a Pythia-2.8B (base model) six-method AxBench-Adv target: the four baselines plus SelfConditioning/SelfConditioningMasked against the project's 400M encoder-decoder pretrain checkpoint, replacing the Qwen-only AxBench-Adv target the config-level hash pins in `configs/eval/axbench_adv/axbench_adv.yaml` had used until now. |
| Baseline-plus-project NL (seven-method) judged model list | `axbench/sweep/nano_gpt_pretrain_steer/baseline_project_nl_evaluate.yaml` | Add the explicitly selected `NLSteering` project method to the six-method baseline-plus-project judge product. The dedicated config keeps the established six-method config byte-for-byte unchanged and prevents an extra result column from implicitly changing the scientific method set. |
| Release per-concept LoRA adapters | `axbench/models/lora.py`, `axbench/scripts/inference.py` | `LoRA.load` calls `PeftModel.from_pretrained(self.model, ...)`, which injects the concept's adapter into the base model in place, and `infer_steering` shares that one model instance across every method and concept of a run; `del benchmark_model` dropped the wrapper but left the adapter modules in the shared model. In a run whose `models` list puts PromptSteering before LoRA (the `[PromptSteering, LoRA]` aux sweeps), PromptSteering for concept k>=1 therefore generated with concept k-1's adapter active (found 2026-11-11: previous-concept words in PromptSteering text rose from 0.0063 to 0.0223 on a Pythia fork, and PromptSteering-only reruns differed by up to 0.26 concept score). `LoRA.release()` now restores the base modules with `PeftModel.unload()` (no merge), and the steering loop calls it after each non-shared method's generation. Only the adapter teardown changes; methods without `release` and the generation itself are unchanged. |
| Chat formatting for SmolLM3-3B and local chat checkpoints | `axbench/utils/constants.py`, `axbench/scripts/train.py`, `axbench/scripts/inference.py`, `axbench/scripts/generate.py`, `axbench/utils/model_utils.py` | `CHAT_MODELS` listed `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B-checkpoints` while runs used `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B`, and a local checkpoint (e.g. a Pythia SFT directory) cannot be listed by name. Training then formatted examples as raw input+output while steering inference always applied the chat template, so trained baselines (LoRA, DiffMean, LinearProbe) saw one format at train time and another at test time. Add `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B` to `CHAT_MODELS`; `is_chat_model_name()` (membership, or `AXBENCH_CHAT_MODEL=1` for a local checkpoint) replaces every former `in CHAT_MODELS` check in train/inference/generate; and `enable_thinking` defaults to `False` for templates that declare the flag, because SmolLM3 otherwise opens about half of its generations with an unclosed `<think>` inside the 128-token budget. Templates without the flag (Qwen, Pythia) render byte-identically; an explicit `enable_thinking` still wins. |
| Opt-in PromptSteering prompt override | `axbench/utils/steering_prompt_override.py`, `axbench/utils/dataset.py` | `AXBENCH_STEERING_PROMPTS_FILE` (a JSON object `{concept: prompt}` covering every requested concept) reuses an earlier run's LM-written steering prompts so only the steered model changes; `AXBENCH_STEERING_PROMPTS_TEMPLATE=1` uses the fixed `T_PROMPT_STEERING` for every concept. With neither set, the LM writes the prompts as before. Used to rerun PromptSteering alone (without the LoRA adapter leak) on the exact prompts of the original runs. |
